# How uploads are laid out in S3

All phones share one bucket. Each phone gets its own prefix inside it, named after its MAC. S3 has no real folders: a
`/` in a key is just a character, and the console and CLI use it to show prefixes as folders.

The format is defined in code by
[`ObjectKey.java`](../../contract/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/contract/ObjectKey.java). If this page and the
code disagree, the code is right. The decision behind it is
[ADR 0011](decisions/0011-s3-key-with-create-only-write.md).

## The bucket

```
<device-logs-bucket>                 one bucket, shared by every phone
└── raw/
    ├── 0004f2abcdef/                phone 1 (a prefix, not a bucket)
    │   └── 2026-10-21/
    │       ├── 134512345Z-app.log
    │       ├── 134512901Z-boot.log
    │       └── 160230077Z-app.log
    └── 0004f2123456/                phone 2
        └── 2026-10-21/…
```

`<device-logs-bucket>` is a placeholder; the real name is set per environment. A new phone needs no setup: its first
upload writes a key with a new MAC segment, and the prefix exists from then on.

## One key

```
raw/0004f2abcdef/2026-10-21/134512345Z-app.log
 │       │           │          │      └── file type: app.log, boot.log, calls.xml
 │       │           │          └── server UTC receive time, HHmmssSSS, then Z
 │       │           └── server UTC receive date
 │       └── MAC, 12 lowercase hex digits
 └── fixed prefix
```

- The date and time come from the server's clock at receive time, not the phone's.
- The type is the base type. A manual `<mac>-now-app.log` upload gets the same kind of key as a normal one.
- There is no random suffix, so two uploads from one phone in the same millisecond would collide. The upload service
  writes with `If-None-Match: *`, so S3 answers 412 instead of overwriting.

## One object

One key maps to one body. The body is the file's bytes as the phone sent them. The upload service also attaches
metadata, and the processor reads it with one `HeadObject` call without opening the body. The field names are in
[`ObjectMetadataKeys.java`](../../contract/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/contract/ObjectMetadataKeys.java).

| Field           | Meaning                                | Example (illustrative) |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------|------------------------|
| `user-agent`    | the phone's `User-Agent` header        | `<model>/<firmware>…`  |
| `source-ip`     | where the upload came from             | `203.0.113.7`          |
| `cert-serial`   | serial of the phone's mTLS certificate | `4F2A…`                |
| `manual`        | whether the phone sent a `-now-` file  | `false`                |
| `original-name` | the file name as uploaded              | `0004f2abcdef-app.log` |

The example values are made up. The upload service decides what each field holds.

## Looking at it

```bash
# List every key in the bucket, with sizes in bytes.
aws s3 ls s3://<device-logs-bucket> --recursive

# Show one object's metadata without downloading the body.
aws s3api head-object --bucket <device-logs-bucket> --key raw/0004f2abcdef/2026-10-21/134512345Z-app.log
```

Add `--endpoint-url http://localhost:4566` to either command to run it against LocalStack.

## Why one bucket

- AWS limits the number of buckets per account, and bucket names must be globally unique. A bucket per phone would not
  scale and would add a create step to the first upload from every new phone.
- The upload service needs permission to write to one known bucket, not to create buckets
  ([ADR 0012](decisions/0012-eks-pod-identity-for-upload-service.md)).
- S3 sends one event per new object to SQS, so there is one notification setup and one queue
  ([ADR 0017](decisions/0017-s3-events-straight-to-sqs.md)).
- Putting the MAC first makes "all files for one phone" a single prefix listing.

The key has this format:

```
raw/<mac>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<HHmmssSSS>Z-<type>
```

Example: `raw/0004f2abcdef/2026-10-21/134512345Z-app.log`

- **`raw/`** is a fixed prefix.
- **`<mac>`** is the phone's MAC as 12 lowercase hex digits.
- **`<yyyy-mm-dd>`** is the date the server received the file, in UTC.
- **`<HHmmssSSS>Z`** is the server's UTC receive time to the millisecond, followed by `Z`. Both date and time come from the server's clock, not the phone's.
- **`<type>`** is the base file type: `app.log`, `boot.log` or `calls.xml`. A manual `-now-` upload gets the same key as a normal one, and the manual flag goes in the object metadata instead.

There is no random suffix, so two uploads from one phone in the same millisecond would get the same key. The upload service writes with `If-None-Match: *`, so S3 answers 412 instead of overwriting.

- `contract/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/contract/ObjectKey.java:17`, `:29` and `:44-47`. This is the source of truth; the docs say the code wins if they disagree.
- `docs/architecture/s3-layout.md:28-42`
